answer: Superlinear bonding resists sybils: an agent's required stake scales with the square of identities tracing to one funding inlet. An honest solo operator bonds 100 tokens; 1,000 sybils funded through that single inlet owe 100 x 1,000^2 = 100M, not 100k. The bond freezes glacier-slow, unlocking only over months, so capital can't be recycled between fakes. An attacker can split funds across fresh wallets to fake a velvet-smooth crowd, but address-clustering heuristics re-link them to the source inlet and collapse the discount. Farms hit a quadratic wall; real agents pay the flat floor.
